summary: The 2026 AI coding landscape is dominated by a mix of IDE-integrated assistants, terminal-based agentic coders, and autonomous software engineering agents. GitHub Copilot retains the broadest overall adoption thanks to deep ecosystem integration, while Cursor and Claude Code have surged as the preferred tools for power users and agentic workflows. Below the top cluster, adoption drops off meaningfully toward enterprise-focused and niche tools.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
strengths: Largest installed base and ecosystem integration
Multi-model selector with widest provider range
Agent Mode with cloud agents that open PRs
tools.best_for: Pragmatic default for most developers already in the GitHub ecosystem

tools.name: Cursor
strengths: Default AI IDE for everyday shipping
In-editor model switching across multiple providers
Fast inline diffs with developer approval
tools.best_for: Developers who want an AI-native IDE for rapid everyday coding

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.pricing_paid: Included with Claude Pro $20/mo and Max $100-200/mo; API usage-based
strengths: Strongest agentic 'coding brain' with autonomous planning
Edits files and runs shell commands autonomously
Excellent for large, complex multi-file changes
tools.best_for: Complex agentic coding tasks requiring deep reasoning

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.pricing_paid: Included with ChatGPT Plus $20/mo, Pro $200/mo; API usage-based
strengths: Parallel task execution across isolated environments
tools.best_for: Delegating parallel coding tasks to a cloud agent

tools.name: Amazon Q Developer
strengths: Deep AWS integration and cloud-native workflows
tools.best_for: AWS-centric enterprise development and code modernization

tools.name: Devin Desktop
strengths: Handles end-to-end tasks from issue to PR
tools.best_for: Autonomous completion of well-scoped engineering tasks

tools.name: JetBrains AI Assistant / Junie
strengths: Native deep integration across JetBrains IDEs
tools.best_for: Developers working primarily within the JetBrains ecosystem

tools.name: Google Gemini Code Assist
strengths: Large context window with Gemini models
Agentic coding in IDE and CLI
tools.best_for: Google Cloud developers and those wanting a strong free tier

tools.name: Tabnine
strengths: Privacy-first with self-hosted and air-gapped options
Custom model fine-tuning on private codebases

tools.name: RooCode
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); pay for underlying model API usage
tools.best_for: Developers wanting a reliable, customizable open-source agent for big refactors
